milestones.title: v0.3.0 - CI and housekeeping
milestones.description: Automated builds and tests, published images, and tidy project settings.

milestones.description: Cleaner dashboard, better alerts behavior, and a layout that works on phones and portrait screens.

milestones.description: Make themes easy to create and share, and give Outpost its own logo and look.

milestones.title: v0.6.0 - Data model and providers

milestones.title: v0.7.0 - Platform

issues.title: Add a CI workflow that builds the image and runs tests on every pull request
issues.body:
## Summary
Automatically check every change so mistakes are caught before they reach main.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggered on pull requests and pushes to `main`
- [ ] Build the Docker image without publishing it
- [ ] Run the Python and JavaScript tests (see the tests issue)
- [ ] Add a status badge to the README
- [ ] Optional: require the check to pass before merging (branch protection)

## Notes
This is a good first pull request for learning the GitHub flow: branch, push, open a PR, watch the check run, merge.

issues.title: Move the ad hoc tests into a tests/ folder
issues.body:
## Summary
Provider and dimming logic was checked with throwaway scripts. Save those checks in the repository so CI can run them.

## Tasks
- [ ] Python tests with the standard `unittest` module (no extra packages) for `nws`, `openmeteo`, `gapfill`, and the updater settings
- [ ] Store sample API responses as fixtures so tests never call the network
- [ ] JavaScript tests for `web/dim.js` using Node's built-in test runner
- [ ] Document how to run everything locally in the README or CONTRIBUTING

## Notes
Fixtures must use made-up coordinates, never a real location.

issues.title: Publish a multi-architecture Docker image to GHCR on version tags
issues.body:
## Summary
Build and publish the image whenever a version tag is pushed, so users can `docker pull` instead of building. Required before an unRAID template.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create `.github/workflows/release.yml` triggered by tags matching `v*`
- [ ] Fail if the tag does not match the contents of the `VERSION` file
- [ ] Build for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (Raspberry Pi) with Buildx and QEMU
- [ ] Publish to `ghcr.io/maxtrax04/outpost` with tags like `0.3.0`, `0.3`, and `latest`
- [ ] Publish an `edge` tag from `main` for early testers
- [ ] Use generated image labels so the version is no longer set by hand in the Dockerfile
- [ ] Make the package public when the repository goes public
- [ ] Document `docker pull` and a `docker run` example

issues.title: Enable Dependabot for the Docker base image and GitHub Actions
issues.body:
## Summary
Get automatic pull requests when the nginx base image or an Action has an update.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `.github/dependabot.yml` with the `docker` and `github-actions` ecosystems on a weekly schedule
- [ ] Pin the nginx base image to a specific version instead of a floating tag
- [ ] Add Python dependencies if any are ever added to `requirements.txt`

issues.title: Create the v0.2.0 tag and GitHub Release
issues.body:
## Summary
Mark the first real release so there is a stable point to point at and a Releases page.

## Tasks
- [ ] Confirm `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` say 0.2.0
- [ ] Create an annotated tag `v0.2.0` and push it
- [ ] Create a GitHub Release from the tag using the changelog text
- [ ] Mark it as a pre-release (the project is before 1.0)

## Notes
See `docs/releasing.md`. Once the release workflow exists, creating the tag will also publish the image.

issues.title: Replace OUTPOST_USER_AGENT with a simple OUTPOST_CONTACT setting
issues.body:
## Summary
Weather services such as NWS and MET Norway ask clients to identify themselves with contact details. Users should only have to provide an email or URL.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `OUTPOST_CONTACT` and build `Outpost/<version> (<contact>)` automatically from the `VERSION` file
- [ ] Warn at startup when a provider that needs contact info is selected and none is set
- [ ] Keep `OUTPOST_USER_AGENT` as an advanced override
- [ ] Update `.env.example`, README, and CHANGELOG

issues.title: Review requirements.txt and trim the Dockerfile
issues.body:
## Summary
All providers use only the Python standard library, so the requirements file may be empty or list unused packages.

## Tasks
- [ ] Check what `requirements.txt` contains and remove anything unused
- [ ] If nothing is needed, remove the pip install step and the pip package to shrink the image
- [ ] If packages are added later, pin exact versions

issues.title: Add CONTRIBUTING.md with workflow, privacy, and IP guidelines
issues.body:
## Summary
Explain how to contribute and set clear rules so the repository stays safe and original.

## Tasks
- [ ] Describe the issue, branch, pull request, and merge workflow (link `docs/github-workflow.md`)
- [ ] Explain how to run the app and tests locally
- [ ] Privacy rule: never post real coordinates, `weather.json`, `.env`, or API keys in issues, pull requests, or screenshots
- [ ] Content rule: only original or properly licensed fonts, icons, and images, listed in `THIRD_PARTY.md`
- [ ] Naming rule: no third-party trademarks, logos, characters, or game artwork in themes or names

issues.title: Say so when a data source does not provide alerts
issues.body:
## Summary
With Open-Meteo the Alerts panel says "No active alerts", but that source never provides alerts. That is misleading.

- [ ] When unsupported, show "Alerts are not provided by this data source" or hide the panel
- [ ] Update tests and docs

issues.title: Add an option to always show the Alerts panel

issues.title: Add nginx security headers, including a Content-Security-Policy
issues.body:
## Summary
A theme is CSS and can load remote files. Restrict what the page may load, and add standard hardening headers.

## Tasks
- [ ] Set a Content-Security-Policy that limits loading to the app itself
- [ ] Add `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy` headers
- [ ] Test all built-in themes, fonts, and icons under the policy
- [ ] Plan the exceptions needed later for the map feature and for embedding in Home Assistant

## Notes
Embedding in Home Assistant needs a matching `frame-ancestors` decision.

issues.title: Design a small HTTP API to replace the file-based flow
issues.body:
## Summary
Today one updater writes one file for one location. Per-viewer locations, multiple locations, and a map proxy need an endpoint such as `/api/weather?lat=..&lon=..`.

## Tasks
- [ ] Choose how to serve it (standard library or a small framework) and weigh the extra dependency
- [ ] Add caching and rate limiting so providers are not overloaded
- [ ] Keep `weather.json` for compatibility
- [ ] Write a short design note before building
